answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable bond before it can trade, and let its reputation grow only from completed, countersigned work over time. A lone knoll of trust is cheap to fake, but a whole field of bonded identities is not: each fake must post its own bond and wait out the same slow history, like layers of shale that cannot be laid down in a whisper. The bond is slashed on proven fraud, so creating thousands of identities costs thousands of bonds while honest agents pay once and keep earning.
